title: Turn a cake out onto a plate: clamp plate and pan together with both hands, turn them over and lift the pan off
instruction: Turn the cake out onto the plate: hold the plate and the pan together, turn them over together, set them on the stand plate side down, then lift the pan off so the cake sits upside down on the plate.
context: Turning a cake out of its tin is done the same way in every kitchen and bakery: a plate goes upside down on the tin, both hands hold plate and tin together from opposite sides, and the two are turned over as one so the cake drops onto the plate; then the tin is lifted off. Held from one side only, the stack hangs off that grip and comes apart, and the plate is far wider than one hand. The same two-handed clamp-and-turn is used to flip trays, moulds and stacked boards.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. A fixed pale blue cake stand, a cylinder 13 cm across and 10 cm tall, stands 30 cm forward on the centre line. On it sits a round grey cake pan (250 g): 14 cm across and 3.6 cm deep inside, with a flat rim 2.5 cm wide around its top (19.6 cm across) and two ears on the rim, 3 cm wide, reaching 13 cm from its centre towards each arm. In the pan is a cake, 12.8 cm across and 2.8 cm tall (160 g), top up, with a dark crust on top. A flat white plate, 21 cm across and 6 mm thick (220 g), lies on the pan's rim, covering it. The pan, the cake and the plate are loose. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Measured from the overhead and wrist videos and with a ruler and a protractor; partial credit is the best reached during the run. 1.0: the plate lies flat on the stand (its middle within 3 cm of the stand's), the cake lies on it upside down (crust down, turned more than 160 degrees) with its middle within 2.5 cm of the plate's, and the pan is off it (the pan's middle 13 cm or more from the cake's), all still for 2 s. 0.5: the cake lies on the plate on the stand like that, but the pan is still over it. 0.25: the cake has been turned upside down while off the table. 0.0: anything else.
reset_notes: Put the pan back on the stand, the cake in it crust up, and the plate on the pan's rim; nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid-body PhysX (Isaac Sim 6.1, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm table. Simplified: the cake is a rigid disc (no crumbs, no sticking to the pan); the pan is one rigid body of a floor, 24 wall and 24 rim panels and two ears; friction is set (pan and plate 0.6, cake 0.7). Dream-1 sees the 320 x 176 frames it expects; the demo video is rendered at 1280 x 720.
